primary.title: IIM-B jumps in Bloomberg MBA rankings
primary.description: Stanford Graduate School of Business has retained the top position in Bloomberg Businessweek’s 2026–27 ranking of US business schools, while IIM Bangalore’s Executive Post Graduate Programme climbed to second place in the Asia-Pacific region.Stanford has now ranked No. 1 in the US for eight consecutive years. The University of Pennsylvania’s Wharton School came second, followed by Harvard Business School and Northwestern University’s Kellogg School of Management.The University of Virginia’s Darden School recorded the biggest rise among the top US schools, moving from 10th place last year to fifth.Also Read| St Gallen tops FT Masters in Management ranking; IIM Ahmedabad leads Indian schoolsDartmouth’s Tuck School ranked sixth and the University of Chicago’s Booth School seventh. UC Berkeley’s Haas School dropped from third to eighth.Cornell’s Johnson School and MIT’s Sloan School tied at ninth. Columbia Business School fell two places to 11th.Top 10 US business schoolsRankBusiness schoolChange from 20251Stanford Graduate School of BusinessNo change2University of Pennsylvania — WhartonNo change3Harvard Business SchoolUp 14Northwestern — KelloggUp 15Virginia — DardenUp 56Dartmouth — TuckNo change7Chicago — BoothNo change8UC Berkeley — HaasDown 59Cornell — JohnsonDown 19MIT — SloanUp 2IIM Bangalore rises to No. 2 in Asia-PacificIIM Bangalore remained India’s highest-ranked programme in the Bloomberg ranking for the fifth consecutive year.Its Executive Post Graduate Programme moved up from third place in 2025 to second in the Asia-Pacific region. Shanghai University of Finance and Economics retained the top position.IIM Bangalore’s overall score rose to 72.6 from 71.7 last year. The programme recorded gains in learning, networking and entrepreneurship, while ranking second in the region for compensation.The ranking is significant for India as IIM Bangalore moved ahead of several established business schools in the Asia-Pacific region. It also highlights the growing presence of Indian management institutes in global MBA rankings.Also Read| India’s higher education moment has arrived just as the world turns inwardTop 5 Asia-Pacific business schools — Bloomberg 2026–27RankBusiness schoolCountry/regionScore1Shanghai University of Finance and EconomicsChina73.62IIM BangaloreIndia72.63Hong Kong University of Science and TechnologyHong Kong71.14Indian School of BusinessIndia70.75Woxsen UniversityIndia63.7Vanderbilt records major jumpVanderbilt University’s Owen School rose 10 places to 17th in the US ranking. Yale School of Management climbed five places to share 12th with Michigan’s Ross School.Duke’s Fuqua School fell five places to 18th, while UNC’s Kenan-Flagler School rose eight places to 20th.Bloomberg assessed schools on compensation, learning, networking and entrepreneurship. It removed the separate inclusion index from the US ranking this year and changed the weight assigned to the remaining categories.The ranking combines feedback from students, alumni and corporate recruiters with employment and salary data.In the Europe and Middle East category, Switzerland’s IMD reclaimed the top position. Ivey Business School returned to the top of the Canadian ranking.
